summary.text: A 31-year-old woman was referred to a neurologist in December 2006 for consciousness disorder and fainting. Her main problems were obesity, snoring and waking with a feeling of suffocation; she was depressed, had sleep apnea and myoclonus, and had several episodes of complete loss of consciousness. Examination showed a large Mallampati class III soft palate and EEG focal dysrhythmia with scattered sharp waves. She was on anticonvulsants (lamotrigine for 5 months, later sodium valproate 500 mg per day) and antidepressants.

Because of a proper facial profile and a large class III soft palate, a minimally invasive procedure was chosen. In May 2007, after lateral cephalogram analysis, craniofacial and pharyngeal airway morphology was evaluated before the surgery. Under general anesthesia, 1 cm of soft palatal mucosa was removed, the tonsils were removed and the tonsillar pillars were sutured together.

Symptoms decreased significantly after recovery, the patient no longer had sleep apnea, and antidepressants and antiepileptic drugs were discontinued; no symptoms of OSA or epilepsy were observed after the surgery. Postoperative EEG showed sharp waves at the level of the trachea, but she was clinically asymptomatic. At 10 years she had no symptoms of sleep apnea or seizure, did not need antiepileptic drugs and had not lost weight.
